ai.description: This small toad reaches 30–35 mm. It is rusty-brown with a pale mid-dorsal stripe and granular skin. Key features include a blunt snout and distinct, enlarged parotoid glands.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ghatophryne rubigina* is uniquely distinguished by the distinct, bright reddish-brown coloration on its dorsal surface, which contrasts with the darker hues of other toads.
ai.habitat: The Kerala Stream Toad inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and rocky stream beds in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kerala Stream Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: Ghatophryne rubigina is an oviparous breeder that lays small clutches of eggs in flowing streams during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ghatophryne rubigina* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits high-elevation rocky stream habitats above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kerala Stream Toad emits a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of rapid, rhythmic pulses, typically heard near fast-flowing rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
